title: Computational Thinking and Simple Programming
summary: The goal of the first year is to have fun and learn how computers 'think' through physical games, puzzles and unplugged activities. The focus is on understanding sequences and cause-and-effect before moving to screens.

semesters.title: Foundations of Logic & Algorithms
semesters.outcomes: Understanding sequences, patterns, and cause-and-effect through unplugged activities. Developing step-by-step instructions for everyday tasks (e.g., making a sandwich) to understand algorithmic thinking.

semesters.title: Digital Creativity & Coding
semesters.outcomes: Applying logic to solve puzzles in games like Lightbot and Scratch Jr, introducing loops and conditionals visually. Creating a simple interactive story or animation using block-based coding, emphasizing creativity and expression.

safety: Introduces the concept of rules in games as analogous to laws and safety guidelines online. Fair play and kindness in digital spaces are emphasized.

title: Raspberry PI: Controlling Inputs and Outputs
summary: The core of the phone—the Raspberry Pi computer—is introduced. Students learn to set up the operating system and write their first Python scripts to control simple electronic circuits.

semesters.title: Hardware Basics & Simple Circuits
semesters.outcomes: Introduction to the Raspberry Pi. Identifying ports (USB, HDMI, GPIO) and setting up the Operating System. Building a simple circuit on a breadboard to light up an LED. Understanding voltage, current, and resistance.

semesters.title: Programming Electronics
semesters.outcomes: Using Python to control the LED (blink, flash patterns). Bridging the gap between software code and physical hardware. Simulating a traffic light sequence using multiple LEDs and Python logic. Introduction to timing and loops.

safety: Basic electrical safety (short circuits). Introduction to the concept that hardware can be controlled by software, and that malicious software could potentially misuse hardware.

title: Phone Specific Components
summary: Focusing on how devices perceive the world, students work with sensors that detect touch, motion, and light. This module lays the groundwork for understanding how phones respond to user environment.

semesters.title: Interaction & Motion Sensors
semesters.outcomes: Implementing capacitive touch sensors. replacing physical buttons with touch interfaces. Interfacing with an Accelerometer/Gyroscope. Detecting tilt and shake gestures.

semesters.title: Environmental Sensing & Integration
semesters.outcomes: Reading light and temperature sensors. Creating automated reactions (e.g., screen auto-brightness). A mini-project combining multiple sensors to log environmental data or control outputs based on gestures.

safety: Privacy implication of sensors: Discussing how apps can track physical activity (steps/motion) and environment. Students learn what data can be inferred from simple sensor readings.

title: Connectivity: Wi-Fi & Bluetooth
summary: The device connects to the world as students explore the invisible networks that link computers. Practical exercises involve scanning for networks and sending messages between devices.

semesters.title: Wireless Networks & Servers
semesters.outcomes: Understanding radio waves. Scanning for Wi-Fi networks and Bluetooth devices using the Pi. Setting up a simple web server on the Pi. Accessing a custom webpage from another device on the same network.

semesters.title: Bluetooth Communication & IoT
semesters.outcomes: Pairing devices and sending simple text strings between them over Bluetooth. Controlling the LEDs/Motors from a smartphone browser over the local Wi-Fi network.

safety: Understanding public vs. private networks. The risks of open Wi-Fi/Bluetooth, 'Bluebugging', and the importance of encryption when sending data over the air.

title: Putting It All Together
summary: The final hardware component—the cellular modem—transforms the computer into a true mobile phone. Students learn how cellular networks function and write scripts to send SMS and make calls.

semesters.title: Cellular Hardware & Communication
semesters.outcomes: What is a Subscriber Identity Module? Connecting a 4G HAT and inserting a SIM. Communicating directly with the modem using standard AT commands. checking signal strength and network status.

semesters.title: SMS & Voice Integration
semesters.outcomes: Writing a script to send and receive text messages programmatically. Initiating a voice call through the Pi. Routing audio to the microphone and speaker.

safety: Metadata retention: Understanding that even if the content of a call is private, the 'who, when, and where' (metadata) is tracked by telecom operators. Spam calls and SMS phishing ('smishing').
